title: File:Altair 8800 Computer.jpg
author: Michael Holley (Commons/en.wikipedia user Swtpc6800)
shows: Front-left three-quarter view of an Altair with a clear Plexiglas top cover (VCF 7.0, 2004, Erik Klein's machine) on top of an 88-DCDD disk drive. Eight cards visible in their slots; per the Commons description, left to right: Seals 8K static RAM, MITS floppy controller (2-board set), MITS floppy controller, two MITS 16K dynamic RAM, MITS 88-2SIO, SSM PROM board, MITS 8080 CPU. Fan and power supply at the rear.
licence_note: Released into the public domain by the photographer, per the Commons file page

title: File:Altair 8800 chasis.jpg
author: Paul jTerrell
shows: Top-down interior with the cover off: three 4-slot expander boards (12 edge connectors, two hand-wired bus jumpers between boards), front-panel board stack standing vertically at the right, power supply (transformers, filter capacitors, fan) at the left, card guides, wiring. No cards installed. Best plan view of the slot layout found.
notes: Uploaded 2026-10-07 by the uploader as own work (Canon PowerShot G2 EXIF, 2002); uploader appears to be Paul Terrell (Byte Shop). Provenance plausible but recent; recheck before use as a texture.

title: File:Altairinside.JPG
author: Joho345
shows: Interior with the top cover off, chassis standing on end in a museum case (Heinz Nixdorf MuseumsForum, Paderborn). Cards removed: shows the stacked expander (backplane) boards with blue card guides and edge connectors, the front-panel display/control boards seen from behind (left, with wiring harness and ribbon cables), the power-supply filter capacitors (3300 uF 16 V) and a hand-wired perfboard card.
licence_note: Released into the public domain by the photographer, per the Commons file page

title: DSC09835
author: kevin (Flickr: believekevin)
shows: Altair with the top cover off, front-left three-quarter view, lamps lit: six or more S-100 cards standing in their slots behind the panel, the front-panel boards and wiring, the transformer and rear panel. Best free view of cards in place in an original box.
notes: Flickr description links a DigiBarn TV episode on Erik Klein; the machine is likely Erik Klein's. Only 800 px available.

title: DSC09844
author: kevin (Flickr: believekevin)
shows: Same machine as DSC09835 from a lower front-left angle: cards in slots, front-panel board wiring, side rail of the chassis.

title: Untitled
author: Marcin Wichary (Flickr: mwichary)
shows: Wider view of the same Heinz Nixdorf MuseumsForum display as Altairinside.JPG: the chassis standing on end with the front panel folded out, backplane stack, ribbon cables, transformer.

title: File:Altair 8800b Computer.jpg
author: Michael Holley (Commons/en.wikipedia user Swtpc6800)
shows: Altair 8800b with the cover off, three-quarter view from front-left: 18-slot motherboard, card guides, two cards installed, transformer and power supply at the rear right, ribbon cables to the front panel.
notes: Different chassis, backplane and power supply from the original 8800; useful only for card mounting and general construction.
licence_note: Released into the public domain by the photographer, per the Commons file page

title: Altair 8800b CPU board, front
author: _brouhaha_ (Flickr: _brouhaha_)
shows: Altair 8800b CPU board, component side, near-orthographic: full card outline, gold edge connector, two regulator heat sinks, the 8080 CPU, crystal, chip positions.
notes: Not the original 88-CPU card (different layout) but the same S-100 outline, so useful for card outline and edge-connector proportions.

shows: Front panel straight-on, high resolution, evenly lit on white: all lamps and switches, legends, blue frame. The lower nameplate strip ('ALTAIR 8800 COMPUTER' on brushed metal) is absent on this unit; the switch bats have coloured tips (red/white/blue/black), unlike most surviving machines.
